verses.1: In that time, Jehovah will become the God of all the families of Israel. And they will be my people.
verses.2: Thus said Jehovah: “Mercy shall be found in the desert by those who are survivors of Haroen, who go there to seek relief for Israel.”
verses.3: From afar, Jehovah appears to me. And with eternal love, I love you. Therefore, I shield you with my grace.
verses.4: Still, your walls stand and are built in the land of Israel. Still, you will be destroyed and emerge from there in a state of despair.
verses.5: Still, I will plant vineyards in the mountains of Shomron. They will be planted and cultivated.
verses.6: For there will be a day when the descendants of Israel will come down from Mount Ebal. They will take their torches and offer them to our God, Jehovah.
verses.7: For thus said Jehovah: “Let Yaakov rejoice and be glad! Let the nations hear his praises. Let them say, ‘Jehovah has saved your people from all their troubles.’”
verses.8: I will bring them from the land of Tzafon. They will be gathered from all over the land. There will be peace and harmony among them. And they will produce a great crowd of children. May they return here again.
verses.9: May they come and be welcomed in their own homes. May they be led to the springs of water, along a proper path. They will not get lost along the way. For I was the father of Israel, and Ephraim was also part of my heritage.
verses.10: Hear the words of the LORD, O nations! Speak from afar away, and say to Israel: “You will be saved, and your name will be preserved as a treasure.”
verses.11: For Jehovah has delivered Jacob from the hands of those who were stronger than us.
verses.12: And they came and rejoiced in the sound of music. They rushed towards the goodness of Jehovah, for the sake of their flocks, their crops, their herds, and their children. Their souls became like a beautiful garden. They no longer sought evil again.
verses.13: Then you will rejoice in the midst of sicknesses and hardships. The old people will also be together, and I will turn their pain into joy and comfort. They will be filled with happiness from their suffering.
verses.14: And I will make the priests’ souls pure and clean. May my people rejoice in their blessings, O LORD!
verses.15: Thus said Jehovah: “A loud cry was heard from the heavens. Rachel wailed over her children. She wept for them, because they were no longer with her.”
verses.16: Thus said Jehovah: “Let your voice be heard from my mouth, and let your eyes be opened, for there will be reward for your efforts.” Let them return from the land of exile.
verses.17: And there will be a call for your descendants. Let the LORD speak, and let the children return to their land.
verses.18: I heard the cries of Ephraim. You have taken me away from them; you prevent me from returning. But I will return, for you are Jehovah, my God.
verses.19: After I was healed again, and after I learned the truth, I questioned my own actions. I also felt ashamed, because I had brought shame upon myself as a young person.
verses.20: O my beloved, give me a son if you can. May he be like those who are mentioned in my words. Let him remember us still. Then may He have mercy on him and save him, O LORD.
verses.21: I have set before you signs and symbols. They will guide your steps along the path of Israel’s return to your city.
verses.22: Until death, they will continue to be afraid of the beautiful woman. For Jehovah has created something new on this land—a beautiful, delicate thing.
verses.23: As Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, has said, “These words shall be spoken in the land of Judah and in its cities again. When they return to their homeland, may Jehovah bless you, O mountain of righteousness!”
verses.24: And they would settle there, along with Judah and all its cities. They would live together as farmers, and they would travel throughout the land.
verses.25: For I have found a weary spirit, and every spirit that causes suffering.
verses.26: So I got up and went out to see what was happening. It was already evening.
verses.27: Look, days are coming, says the Lord. I have sown the seed in the house of Israel and in the house of Judah. It is the seed of man and the seed of animals.
verses.28: And just as I have planned to destroy them, to tear them apart, to devastate them, to take away what belongs to them… So too, I will destroy them by causing them to be destroyed. May the LORD do so!
verses.29: In those days, no longer would fathers say that they ate with their wives and sons.
verses.30: For if a man dies in his sin, all those who eat his forbidden food will also be punished.
verses.31: Now, days are coming, says the LORD. I will destroy the house of Israel and the house of Judah, in a new covenant.
verses.32: It is not a covenant that I have made with their ancestors on the day I took them into my hands to bring them out of Egypt. Those ancestors broke my covenant, and I became their master. May the LORD have mercy on them.
verses.33: For this is the covenant that I made with the house of Israel after those days. “Now, says the LORD, I will give you My Torah; it will be written in their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
verses.34: And no one shall teach his neighbor or his brother, “Know Jehovah!” For they all know Me from childhood until old age. May Jehovah be praised! For He forgives their sins and remembers their transgressions no more.
verses.35: Thus said Jehovah: “Let there be light in the night, with laws and stars that shine in the darkness. Let the sea be calm, and let its waves be still.” Thus said Jehovah, the Almighty.
verses.36: If these laws were abolished by me, then say, “Lord, let the descendants of Israel also be able to settle down as a nation before me, just as they have always been.”
verses.37: So said the LORD: “If the heavens are destroyed from above, and if those who rule over the earth are questioned from below, then I will also punish every branch of Israel for all that they have done, as the LORD has said.”
verses.38: See, days are coming, says the LORD. The city will be built for the LORD, from the hill of Hananel, the gate of the Finis.
verses.39: And again, the wind blew against him, over the heights of Garib.
verses.40: And all those ruins and debris, along with all the dead bodies, will remain there until they reach the river Kedron. Until Pinnat Sh’ar Hossim is reached from the east, which is a holy place for God. They will not be destroyed or damaged ever again.
